t.6.63.1: When that dreadful, tumultuous battle had begun, bringing destruction upon heroic men, Aṅgada, eager for combat, attacked the hero Kampana.
t.6.63.2: Kampana, having first challenged Aṅgada, swiftly struck him in his rage with a mace; and he, violently struck, staggered.
t.6.63.3: Having regained consciousness, that powerful one hurled a mountain peak, and Kampana, struck by the blow, fell to the ground.
t.6.63.4: Then the army of the lord of the rākṣasas, its foremost heroes slain and itself distressed, went toward where the son of Kumbhakarṇa stood. As that army came rushing on with great speed, Kumbha comforted it.
t.6.63.5: Grasping his bow, he, the foremost of archers, fully composed, released arrows resembling venomous serpents, arrows that tear apart the body.
t.6.63.6: That supreme bow of his, with its arrow set upon it, shone all the more, radiant like a second bow of Indra gleaming with lightning and Airāvata.
t.6.63.7: Then, with that feathered arrow, golden-shafted and clothed in plumes, drawn back to the ear and released, he struck Dvivida.
t.6.63.8: Struck suddenly by him, that best of monkeys, resembling a mountain peak, lost his footing and, writhing and bewildered, fell down.
t.6.63.9: But Mainda, seeing his brother broken there in the great battle, seized a huge rock and rushed forward with speed.
t.6.63.10: The mighty one hurled that rock at the rākṣasa, but Kumbha shattered it with five gleaming arrows.
t.6.63.12: But Mainda, the leader of the monkey troops, struck by him with that blow upon a vital spot, fell to the ground senseless.
t.6.63.11: Fitting another sharp-tipped arrow, like a venomous serpent, the greatly splendid one struck the elder brother of Dvivida in the chest.
t.6.63.13: Seeing those two mighty maternal uncles of his fallen, Aṅgada rushed with great speed at Kumbha, who held his bow raised.
t.6.63.14: As he came rushing on, Kumbha pierced him with five iron arrows and with three other sharp shafts, as one strikes an elephant with lances.
t.6.63.15: The mighty Kumbha pierced Aṅgada with arrows of many kinds, sharp and keen, their edges unblunted and adorned with gold.
t.6.63.16: Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, though his limbs were pierced, did not tremble; he rained down showers of rocks and trees upon his head.
t.6.63.17: The glorious son of Kumbhakarṇa cut to pieces all those hurled by the son of Vālin, and again he shattered the rocks.
t.6.63.18: And seeing the leader of the monkey troops rushing toward him, Kumbha pierced him between the brows with two arrows, as one strikes an elephant with two firebrands.
t.6.63.19: Aṅgada, covering with one hand his two eyes that were drenched with blood, seized with his other hand a sāla tree standing nearby.
t.6.63.20: Him, as he hurled with great force a tree that was like Indra's banner and resembled Mount Mandara, while all the Rākṣasas looked on.
t.6.63.21: He pierced him with seven sharp arrows that rend the body. Aṅgada was racked with pain again and again; he sank down and swooned.
t.6.63.23: But Rāma, hearing that the son of Vālin was distressed in the great battle, then commanded the foremost of the monkeys, headed by Jāmbavant.
t.6.63.22: Seeing the formidable Aṅgada distressed, like one sinking in the ocean, the foremost of the monkeys reported him to Rāghava.
t.6.63.24: Those tigers among the monkeys, having heard Rāma's command, rushed in great fury upon Kumbha, who held his bow raised.
t.6.63.26: Jāmbavān, Suṣeṇa and the monkey Vegadarśī, enraged, rushed together upon the heroic son of Kumbhakarṇa.
t.6.63.25: Then the bull-like monkeys, trees and rocks in their hands and eyes red with anger, rushed toward Aṅgada, eager to protect him.
t.6.63.27: Seeing those mighty ones rushing at him from the lord of the monkeys, he held them back with a flood of arrows, as a mountain hems in a lake.
t.6.63.28: Having met his mass of arrows, the great-souled lords of the monkeys could not pass beyond it, just as the great ocean cannot pass beyond its shore.
t.6.63.29: But seeing those hosts of monkeys tormented by showers of arrows, the lord of the monkeys placed Aṅgada, his brother's son, behind him.
t.6.63.30: In the battle Sugrīva rushed swiftly upon Kumbha, as a swift lion rushes upon an elephant roaming the ridges of a mountain.
t.6.63.31: And the mighty one, uprooting great mountains, many aśvakarṇa and dhava trees, and various other trees, hurled them.
t.6.63.32: That irresistible shower of trees, covering the sky, the glorious son of Kumbhakarṇa cut to pieces with his sharpened arrows.
t.6.63.33: Studded with sharp arrows by the fierce Kumbha, who took careful aim, those trees shone like dreadful śataghnīs.
t.6.63.34: But seeing that shower of trees cut down by Kumbha, the valiant and glorious lord of the monkeys, great in spirit, was not shaken.
t.6.63.35: Though suddenly pierced, he endured those arrows, then seized Kumbha's bow, which shone like the rainbow, and broke it.
t.6.63.36: Then, having swiftly leapt down after accomplishing a most difficult feat, he angrily spoke to Kumbha, who stood like an elephant with broken tusks.
t.6.63.37: O elder brother of Nikumbha, your valor and that wondrous speed of your arrows, your modesty and your might are found either in you or in Rāvaṇa alone.
t.6.63.38: O you who are equal to Prahrāda, Bali, the slayer of Vṛtra, Kubera and Varuṇa, you alone have been born after your father's likeness, and are even mightier than him.
t.6.63.40: By virtue of a granted boon, your paternal uncle withstands the Devas and Dānavas; but Kumbhakarṇa, by his own valor, withstands both the Suras and the Asuras.
t.6.63.39: The gods cannot overcome you alone, mighty-armed subduer of foes with spear in hand, just as mental afflictions cannot overcome one who has conquered his senses.
t.6.63.41: In archery you are equal to Indrajit, and in prowess equal to Rāvaṇa; today, by virtue of your strength and valour, you are the foremost of the rākṣasas in the world.
t.6.63.42: Today let all beings witness the wondrous great clash between you and me in battle, like that of Śakra and Śambara.
t.6.63.43: An incomparable deed has been done, and your skill in weapons has been displayed; and these heroic monkeys of fearsome valor have been struck down by you.
t.6.63.44: Out of fear of reproach as well, O hero, you are not slain by me, for you have done your deed and are exhausted; once you are rested, behold my strength.
t.6.63.46: Then Kumbha, leaping up and rushing at Sugrīva, struck him in anger on the chest with his fist, which had the force of a thunderbolt.
t.6.63.45: Honored by those words of Sugrīva, though they were tinged with contempt, his energy blazed up like that of a fire into which clarified butter has been poured.
t.6.63.47: His skin burst open and blood sprang forth from him, and that fist of mighty force struck against the circle of his bones.
t.6.63.48: Then, through the force of the impact, a blaze flared up there again and again, like the flame born from the crushing blow of a thunderbolt upon Mount Meru.
t.6.63.49: Struck there by him, Sugrīva, the bull among monkeys, of great strength, clenched his fist, which was like a thunderbolt.
t.6.63.50: The mighty one brought down his fist, blazing with a thousand flames and radiant as the orb of the sun, upon the chest of Kumbha.
t.6.63.51: Struck by him with his fist, the rākṣasa quickly fell down, like the blazing-rayed Lohitāṅga dropping from the sky by chance.
t.6.63.52: The form of Kumbha, falling with his chest shattered by the fist, shone like the form of the sun, lord of rays, when assailed by Rudra.
t.6.63.53: When he was slain in battle by that bull among monkeys of terrible prowess, the earth with its mountains and forests shook, and fear entered the rākṣasas all the more.
